admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.collection_rel: Asks the metadata source which saga each movie belongs to and links it. Only runs when an admin starts it.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.compat_downloa: Prepares a copy for a phone that cannot play the original audio track: the picture is copied as is, the sound converted to stereo. Only runs when a user starts a download.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.complexity_cla: Samples a few frames of each video to measure how much motion it carries. Used to pick transcoding bitrates that suit the content. Runs continuously over the library.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.intro_detectio: Finds the intros and end credits of episodes (sound shared across the season, file chapters). Feeds the Skip Intro button. Runs continuously and pauses while something is playing.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.keyframe_backf: Reads each file's seek index (keyframe positions) and checks that its frame rate is constant. Lets the video be sent as is, without transcoding. Runs continuously, after the video details refresh.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.level_backfill: Re-reads the technical details of files already in the library (H.264/HEVC profile, HDR, Dolby Vision, interlacing of old rips). Lets the video be sent without transcoding and avoids wrong colours. Runs continuously and pauses while something is playing.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.library_scan: Walks the library folders and analyses new or changed files so they show up. Runs at startup, periodically, and as soon as a file changes.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.reduced_downlo: Prepares a lighter 720p copy when the original file is too large for the device. Only runs when a user starts a download.
admin.activity.bgTaskHelp.trickplay_gene: Generates the thumbnails shown while dragging the seek bar (one frame every 7 seconds). Runs when media is added, and at startup for items that have none yet.
admin.activity.exportTruncated: Export stopped at the maximum of {{max}} rows; {{total}} exist. Narrow the range and export again.

admin.calibration.av1Hint: Encode to AV1 when a client supports it - better compression. Hardware-only; software AV1 is never used for streaming.
admin.calibration.av1NoHw: No AV1 hardware encoder detected - turning this on has no effect (streams stay H.264).
admin.calibration.benchmarkingLine: Calibrating now - about 2 minutes. New playbacks are held off until it is done.
admin.calibration.cardSubtitle: Measured at boot - sets the cap on the HLS ladder so the host doesn't overshoot what it can encode in realtime.
admin.calibration.contendedLine: Provisional: the server was already busy when it measured itself (CPU at {{percent}}%), so these ceilings are underestimated - they describe a shared machine, not this one. It will measure again on its own once idle.
admin.calibration.hwEnabledHint: Encoding on the GPU when possible
admin.calibration.hwFallbacksDesc: Recent hardware encodes that fell back automatically - the host keeps playing via software while the cause is recorded. Recalibrate once the hardware is fixed.
admin.calibration.lowPowerHint: Intel's fixed-function encoder (VDEnc): less GPU load and power, but no B-frames on older iGPUs and a simpler rate control, so slightly lower quality at the same bitrate. Leave it off unless the GPU is saturated.
admin.calibration.maxBitrateHint: Each rung is encoded at the source bitrate scaled to its resolution, never below the ladder's floor. Set a ceiling if remote viewers buffer.
admin.calibration.maxBitrateRemoteHint: Applied to clients outside your private network. "Follow the LAN" adds no remote-specific cap, so a high-bitrate remux can go out unless another limit applies. A per-user limit stays the tightest one.
admin.calibration.maxBitrateRemoteNone: Follow the LAN (no extra remote cap)
admin.calibration.pendingLine: Waiting for a quiet moment to calibrate ({{reason}}): the server measures itself only once nothing else is running, so the ceilings below are interim. Use "Recalibrate" to run it now.
admin.calibration.pendingReason.accelera: an accelerator was detected but never measured
admin.calibration.recalibrateHint: Re-run the benchmark after enabling hardware acceleration, swapping the CPU, or migrating the container to a different host.
admin.calibration.setupSubtitle: Measuring how high your host can encode in realtime. This usually takes ~20 seconds and only runs once.
admin.calibration.transcodesActiveToast: Stop active playback before recalibrating - the benchmark needs an idle host to measure the true ceiling.
admin.calibration.wslVaapiNote: VAAPI/QSV go through Mesa's d3d12 driver on WSL and can't sustain transcoding here - use NVENC, or validate VAAPI on a native Linux host.

admin.loadtest.appAmplificationLine: Of which {{app}}x is asked for by the server itself: anything beyond that is the kernel reading ahead into data nobody wanted.
admin.loadtest.coldCacheHint: Keeps evicting the library from the system's cache for the whole run. Closer to real use when the library is too big to sit in memory - expect a lower, more honest viewer count.
admin.loadtest.coldCacheLine: The library was evicted from the system's cache throughout: these figures measure the storage, not the RAM. Never compare them with a warm run.
admin.loadtest.coldCacheStillStarvedLine: Warning: the disk counter still saw almost nothing, despite the cache being evicted throughout. On this mount the kernel cannot see the reads (a network or 9p/virtiofs path), or a cache outside this system (a VM host, a NAS controller) is absorbing them. These figures measure that delivery path, not the disks.
admin.loadtest.coldCacheToggle: Cold cache: measure the storage, not the RAM
admin.loadtest.diskAtAudienceLine: But with {{viewers}} viewers, that same storage gives only {{rate}} (peak {{peak}}, reached at just {{readers}} readers). It is not running out of bytes, it is running out of heads: the disk is on its knees, not at 40%.
admin.loadtest.diskCeilingLine_one: Media read throughput, measured on this server: {{rate}} (across {{count}} disk).
admin.loadtest.diskCeilingLine_other: Media read throughput, measured on this server: {{rate}} ({{count}} disks read in parallel).
admin.loadtest.errorActiveStreams: Playback is currently active - the test refuses to run over real viewers.
admin.loadtest.errorGeneric: Could not start the load test.
admin.loadtest.harnessCpuLine: {{pct}}% of the measured CPU was the load generator itself: it has been subtracted from the figures above.
admin.loadtest.heading: Load test
admin.loadtest.idleDescription: Measure what this server can sustain with real simulated viewers.
admin.loadtest.idleWarning: Run this only when nobody is watching - the server refuses to start over real playback.
admin.loadtest.noBottleneckHint: No resource ran out: the box likely holds more. Raise the ceiling and run again.
admin.loadtest.noCeilingLine: The run climbs until a resource gives out - there is no viewer ceiling.
admin.loadtest.perViewerLine: Cost of one more viewer: {{cpu}}% CPU, {{mem}} memory, {{disk}} disk read, {{net}} throughput.
admin.loadtest.predictedLine: Transcoding: {{measured}} streams held, ~{{count}} predicted by calibration (calibration only ever predicts transcodes, never direct play).
admin.loadtest.readAmplificationLine: Warning: the server reads {{ratio}}x more bytes from disk than it serves. It saturates its storage on data it throws away - halving this ratio would double the audience, on the very same hardware.
admin.loadtest.reportHeadline_one: This server sustains {{count}} simultaneous viewer in {{scenario}}.
admin.loadtest.reportHeadline_other: This server sustains {{count}} simultaneous viewers in {{scenario}}.
admin.loadtest.resourcesLine: Consumed at that tier: CPU {{cpu}}% (peak {{cpuPeak}}%), memory {{mem}} of {{memLimit}}, disk read {{disk}}, served {{net}}.
admin.loadtest.segmentLine: Segment fetch: {{p50}} ms typical, {{p95}} ms worst.
admin.loadtest.servedFromCacheLine: Warning: the disk barely moved - everything was served from the operating system's cache. The library fits in RAM, which it will not in real use: this viewer count is overstated, sometimes several times over.
admin.loadtest.sharedCacheLine_one: {{count}} of them served straight from the shared cache.
admin.loadtest.sharedCacheLine_other: {{count}} of them served straight from the shared cache.
admin.loadtest.skippedCandidatesLine_one: {{count}} title not eligible for mkvgo was skipped.
admin.loadtest.skippedCandidatesLine_oth: {{count}} titles not eligible for mkvgo were skipped.
admin.loadtest.sloByTypeLine: Stall threshold, one per playback path: {{parts}}
admin.loadtest.slowestDiskLine: The slowest drive only gives {{rate}}: viewers landing on a film that lives there are the first to suffer.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.admissionFull: The server refused the next viewer, as designed.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.cpuSaturated: The CPU saturated: that is what limits this server.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.error: An error stopped the test early.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.libraryLimit: No usable title in the library for this scenario.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.memorySaturate: Memory saturated: that is what limits this server.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.serverFailing: The server stopped serving viewers under this load.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.sloBreach: Playback would have started stalling beyond this point.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.startupTooSlow: Starting a new stream became too slow: the server is full, even though it keeps feeding the others.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.throughputSatu: Throughput flattened out: the server cannot read the media any faster. That is the bottleneck.
admin.loadtest.stopReason.tokenExpired: Session expired - log back in and try again.
admin.loadtest.storageCollapseLine: Warning: the storage collapses past {{count}} concurrent reads - throughput falls away and a single read starts taking seconds. It is the storage, not the server, that caps how many people can watch.
admin.loadtest.storageOpaqueColdLine: The library sits on a {{fs}} mount. Cold cache was applied to the mount, but the disks underneath may keep serving from their own cache, and the server's kernel cannot see the reads behind it (blind disk counter, a pool counts as a single disk). These figures are colder than a warm run, not a measure of the disks.
admin.loadtest.storageOpaqueLine: The library sits on a {{fs}} mount. The server's kernel cannot see the reads behind it, so the disk counter stays blind and a pool counts as a single disk: the storage figures describe this delivery path, not the disks.
admin.loadtest.throughputCeilingLine: Throughput flattened at {{rate}}: the server cannot read the media any faster. That is the bottleneck.
admin.loadtest.ttffLine: Startup time: {{p50}} ms typical, {{p95}} ms worst case.

admin.qoe.overrides.resetHint: Drop this adaptive cap immediately. The worker will re-evaluate on the next tick.
admin.qoe.overrides.subtitle: Automatic adjustments based on how playback actually goes (buffering, throughput), on top of the calibrated ceiling. Each row temporarily lowers the maximum quality for one kind of source until it expires.

admin.repairHistory.empty: Nothing has ever been done to this file.
admin.repairHistory.evidenceDeclared: Acted on what the file declared about itself, without measuring.
admin.repairHistory.evidenceMeasured: Measured: the file's own audio tracks were {{lag}}s apart, confidence {{confidence}}.
admin.repairHistory.intro: Evey keeps no copy of a repaired file. This journal is the record of every change to its bytes - and, for the ones whose inverse is exact, the way back.
admin.repairHistory.notReversible: Nothing here can be undone: the last change either discarded bytes, which no record brings back, or left the picture and sound untouched.
admin.repairHistory.title: What was done to {{title}}
admin.repairHistory.undoHint: Applies the exact opposite of the recorded shift. Nothing is re-encoded, and it can be undone again.
admin.repairJournal.empty: No repair touched a file in this window.
admin.repairJournal.intro: Every change a repair made to a file's bytes, across the whole library, newest first. What a batch touched is answered here, not by guessing from file dates.
admin.repairJournal.title: Repair journal
admin.seekIndex.ackDone: Marked as seen - it stays out of the list until the file changes
admin.seekIndex.allGood: Nothing awaits you - every scanned file is healthy or acknowledged.
admin.seekIndex.audioOffsetHint: An audio track starts after the picture. That is how a dub is lined up with a cut, and every player follows it - nothing to fix here.
admin.seekIndex.audioOffsetProvenHint: An audio track starts after the picture, and this file's own tracks were compared and agree: the offset is deliberate. Nothing to do.
admin.seekIndex.audioPictureOffHint: Measured on the file's own subtitles (timed to the picture): audio track {{track}} sits {{sec}}s from where the speech should be - positive means the sound must move later. Two or more windows of the film agreed. Check it on the preview clip and apply that shift from there; nothing is rewritten on its own.
admin.seekIndex.audioShortHint: An audio track stops {{sec}}s before the video does (silent credits on that track). The file is otherwise healthy and playback fills the missing tail with silence. Measured against where the picture actually ends, not against the container's declared duration - so an over-stated duration is never blamed on the audio. No repair can help: the audio simply is not in the file; re-acquire the source for a real fix.
admin.seekIndex.audioTrackZeroedHint: One audio track of this file starts exactly on the picture while another keeps its small original offset. That is the mark an earlier audio repair leaves when it pulls a track back by its own declared delay. If the dub plays early, the amount removed is no longer in the file and nothing here can put it back automatically: listen, correct it by hand, or re-acquire the file.
admin.seekIndex.audioTracksDisagreeHint: This file's audio tracks were compared and drift {{sec}}s apart, so one of them sits in the wrong place. Nothing here can tell which, so nothing is changed automatically: play both and keep the good one, or re-acquire the file.
admin.seekIndex.brokenInterleaveHint: The tracks are stored in separate blocks of minutes (video alone, then audio alone) instead of side by side - a timestamp steps back {{sec}}s between two points of the file. Every header is fine and every stream decodes, but no sequential player gets past the first block: direct play stalls and ffmpeg waits minutes for its first audio segment. Only the packager (streaming without conversion) serves it, reading about twice the file and a whole block at each seek. The Re-mux button rewrites it losslessly (the original is kept as backup); a plain stream copy elsewhere reproduces the layout.
admin.seekIndex.description: A read-only scan gives every MKV/WebM file one verdict, and there are only two.
admin.seekIndex.emptyDescription: Pick a library and scan to find MKV/WebM files without a seek index.
admin.seekIndex.fixContainerHint: This .mkv is really an MP4/MOV: the server renames it to .mp4 and updates the library entry. Nothing is rewritten.
admin.seekIndex.fixContainerStarted: Rename started in the background - progress below
admin.seekIndex.introDetailRemarks: On the "for information" side: an incomplete download, keyframes too sparse to seek into, an offset between audio tracks, a shorter audio track, surplus bytes after the end.
admin.seekIndex.introDetailScope: Every repaired file keeps its original as a .mkvgobak backup, restorable at any time.
admin.seekIndex.introInformational: what we noticed and cannot fix here. Mark them as seen and the page empties out.
admin.seekIndex.introRepairable: missing seek index, corrupted stretch, .mkv that is really an MP4. Repair all handles them in one run.
admin.seekIndex.jobCancelHint: Stops at the next file: the file in progress is finished or restored, never left half-written.
admin.seekIndex.jobCancelRequested: Stop requested - the job ends after the current file
admin.seekIndex.jobCompletedSkipped: {{kind}} finished - {{done}} file(s) repaired, {{skipped}} skipped (nothing to do)
admin.seekIndex.jobReadOnlyHint: Some files are on a read-only volume. Remount your media folders read-write (remove :ro in docker-compose) and restart the containers, then retry.
admin.seekIndex.jobSkippedHint: Files the job looked at and left untouched - already in the target state, or beyond what this repair can do. They are counted in "processed".
admin.seekIndex.keepBackupsHint: A .mkvgobak of every repaired file survives the job so you can roll back anytime - costs one extra copy per file on disk.
admin.seekIndex.keepBackupsOffHint: No backup is left behind: only the last {{n}} are kept during the run and removed at the end, and each repair is deep-verified in exchange. Choose this on a tight disk.
admin.seekIndex.noEbml: No MKV/WebM files in this scope - other containers don't need a seek index.
admin.seekIndex.onlyAttention: Only show what awaits an action or a look
admin.seekIndex.paceFastHint: Several files at once, no pause: on a library spread over several disks this is about three times quicker, but the disks are busy for the whole run and playback may stutter.
admin.seekIndex.paceGentleHint: One file at a time, then a pause as long as reading it took: the disks stay free about half the time. Slower, but the right choice if someone needs to keep watching something while the scan runs.
admin.seekIndex.purgeAllConfirm_one: Permanently delete {{count}} backup file (.mkvgobak)? Roll back first if a repaired file misbehaves - after this there is no undo.
admin.seekIndex.purgeAllConfirm_other: Permanently delete {{count}} backup files (.mkvgobak)? Roll back first if a repaired file misbehaves - after this there is no undo.
admin.seekIndex.readOnlyNote: Repairing writes to your media folders. If they are mounted read-only (:ro in docker-compose), remount them read-write and restart the containers first - scanning still works.
admin.seekIndex.reinterleaveHint: The server re-writes the file with its tracks side by side (stream copy, nothing re-encoded) and proves the copy carries every packet before swapping it in. The original stays next to it as a backup.
admin.seekIndex.reinterleaveStarted: Re-mux started in the background - progress below
admin.seekIndex.repairAllConfirm_one: Repair {{count}} file in the background? Missing indexes are rebuilt and mislabelled containers are renamed to .mp4 - every rewritten file is verified then swapped atomically. This is a LONG operation: it rewrites files and can take hours.
admin.seekIndex.repairAllConfirm_other: Repair {{count}} files in the background? Missing indexes are rebuilt and mislabelled containers are renamed to .mp4 - every rewritten file is verified then swapped atomically. This is a LONG operation: it rewrites files and can take hours.
admin.seekIndex.repairHint: Rebuilds the seek index. Safe by construction: rewritten to a temp copy, fully re-validated (tracks, duration, real on-disk index), then swapped in with an atomic rename - the original is kept as a .mkvgobak you can roll back to, and any failed check refuses the swap and leaves the file untouched.
admin.seekIndex.repairResyncHint: For a file a normal repair refused (corrupted region): the tolerant rewrite skips the damaged span and resynchronises - everything before and after is recovered, only the damaged bytes are lost. Always keeps a backup.
admin.seekIndex.repairStarted: Repair started in the background - progress shows below
admin.seekIndex.resyncDamagedHint: Their index is fine but a corrupted stretch makes them unplayable. Resync skips it - those bytes are lost for good - and always keeps the original as a backup, whatever the choice below.
admin.seekIndex.resyncRequiredHint: The normal repair walked this file and its stream does not parse: a corrupted region the scan, which only reads the header, could not have seen. Only a resync gets past it - it skips the region and loses those bytes for good, always keeping the original as a backup. How much is lost is not known in advance here.
admin.seekIndex.resyncRequiredNote: Including {{count}} the normal repair refused: their corruption was only found by rewriting them, so what they lose is not part of the figure above.
admin.seekIndex.rollbackAllConfirm_one: Restore {{count}} file from its .mkvgobak backup? This undoes prior repairs in the selected scope.
admin.seekIndex.rollbackAllConfirm_other: Restore {{count}} files from their .mkvgobak backups? This undoes prior repairs in the selected scope.
admin.seekIndex.rollbackStarted: Restore started in the background - progress shows below
admin.seekIndex.scanStarted: Scan started - it runs in the background, progress shows below
admin.seekIndex.searchPlaceholder: Search a title or a path
admin.seekIndex.seekCoarseHint: The index was rebuilt and a hole remains: {{detail}}. A seek INTO that hole lands at its edge; everywhere else seeking is exact. Measured live, the hole is most often the final credits (no keyframe after the last one), which no index can fix and which matters to nobody. A hole in the middle of the film is the encode's own keyframes - a better source is the only cure.
admin.seekIndex.seekCoarseNoDetail: the cues stay too far apart at one point
admin.seekIndex.statsInformationalHint: A measurement can be wrong - if the file plays fine, it is fine.
admin.seekIndex.title: Media Health
admin.seekIndex.trailingJunkHint: Surplus bytes lie after the declared end of the Segment - the media is complete and plays fine. Nothing to do: a rewrite for another repair drops them in passing.
admin.seekIndex.truncatedHint: This file is an incomplete download: its last bytes never arrived and no tool can recover them - it plays fine up to the cut, then stops. Re-acquire the source for a complete copy; no repair applies, so none is offered.

admin.serverConfig.artworkDesc: Cache posters and other artwork locally on the server.
admin.serverConfig.artworkInfo: When off, the frontend depends on external CDN URLs that some browsers block (Firefox's Opaque Response Blocking, for instance). Caching locally also lets the server normalise the format to WebP.

admin.serverConfig.backgroundJobs.pauseB: Suspends background transcoding-related jobs while a stream is active, so they don't compete with playback for disk I/O and CPU.
admin.serverConfig.backgroundJobs.restar: These flags are read once at server startup. Saving a change here has no effect on the running server - you must restart it for the new value to take effect.
admin.serverConfig.backgroundJobs.snapsh: Uses the mkvgo fast decoder for timeline preview thumbnails. Turning this off falls back to the exact ffmpeg decoder only.

admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.applyHint: Applies to the next item, no restart needed.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.globalDesc: Every background task draws from this share of the CPU capacity. 25 % keeps the box responsive; 50 % is a boost for when nobody is using it. Playback always comes first: a task pauses while someone is watching.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.subtitle: How much of the processor the background work may take together: scans, thumbnails, intro detection, classification.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.tasks.compl: Sample encodes that grade each title for the transcoding ladder.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.tasks.intro: Episodes and movies analysed at once for intro, recap and credits.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.tasks.libra: Probing, chapters and serving plan of the files a library scan finds.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.tasks.trick: Decoder threads of the timeline thumbnails' generation.
admin.serverConfig.cpuBudget.tasksDesc: A heavy task may get a share of its own, which replaces the global one for that task. Shares never stack: everything running in the background stays under the highest share set here.

Primary - TheIntroDB (theintrodb.org): movies + TV, free API key required. Fallback - IntroDB (introdb.app): TV episodes only, no key required.
